newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Italy PM pledges support for Romania's NATO bid.
newsitem.headline: Italy PM pledges support for Romania's NATO bid.

text.p: Visiting Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Monday pledged Rome's firm support for Romania's goal of early admission to NATO.
"We want NATO to expand not only to the north, but also to the south of Europe," Prodi told journalists after talks with his Romanian counterpart Victor Ciorbea.
"Our decision to support Romania's admission bid is firm and irrevocable," he said.

Italy, France and other southern NATO members, as well as Canada, have openly backed Romania's drive to get invited, along with Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, when the Alliance announces its first eastward expansion at a July summit in Madrid.
But the United States, Britain and Germany have been lukewarm in declaring their support for Romania so far.
Ciorbea hailed Italy's support for his country's admission among the first former East bloc states, which he said would "weigh heavy when a decision on NATO's enlargement is made in Madrid".
Bucharest, seeking to boost its image as a haven of stability in the volatile Balkans, has deployed 400 Romanian troops as part of the Italian-led security force in Albania.
Prodi, the first Italian Prime Minister to visit here in 20 years, was accompanied on his one-day trip by a large group of Italian company executives.
Bucharest's new leaders have vowed to privatise key state-owned industries, including communications, road building, and the energy and defence sectors.

"Our strategic interest is to work with Italy to build road links from central Europe, via Bucharest, to the Black Sea, and from the southern Balkans, via Bucharest, to Kiev, in Ukraine," Ciorbea said.

Attracting foreign investors to Romania -- which has drawn only one-tenth of the money injected into neighbouring Hungary in the post-communist era -- is a plank of the reforms pledged by the centrists, who ousted the ex-communists in last November's elections.
